title: $\RHom$ preserves bounded constructible complexes ($\ell$-adic $\Lambda$)
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be one of $\underline{\cO}_E$, $\underline E$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite;
[sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) or $\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]), and let $X$
be a scheme of the setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. If $K,L\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ are bounded
constructible ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), then so is $\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(K,L)$
([sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]).

external.place: Since $K$ is bounded constructible, reduction modulo $\varpi$ gives $$ \RHom(K,L)/\varpi\cong\RHom_{\cO_E/\varpi}(K/\varpi,L/\varpi). $$ By Deligne's finiteness theorem for the internal $\RHom$ (SGA 4½, *Th. finitude*, 1.6) on the finite type $k$-scheme $X$, with coefficients in which $p$ is invertible, this is a bounded complex with constructible cohomology.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

The cases $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ follow by inverting $\ell$ and by descending to a finite extension $E$ ([sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit]), as in [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves]; see Bhatt–Scholze, §6.8.

proof.text: Use the proved ell-adic Serre theorem to make bounded constructibility triangulated and isomorphism invariant. For every constructible F and degree n, the fixed-first-argument functor RHom(F[n],-) is triangulated by tensor-Hom adjunction, with its canonical shift compatibility. Finite truncation devissage in the second input reduces it to the single-sheaf internal-Hom calculation. For arbitrary first input K, induct on a bounded cohomological interval. The empty interval is zero, whose internal Hom is zero by tensor-Hom currying. In the successor step truncate at the top degree b; the top term is one constructible sheaf in degree b and the lower term has shorter amplitude. The proved distinguished internal-Hom triangle reverses these terms and triangle closure yields RHom(K,L). This induction requires no unproved first-variable shift comparison.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3); first-variable finite amplitude induction and second-variable triangulated devissage
